[WP] a LARP in the remote wilderness suddenly stumbles upon extremely real magic.

"I move through the forest, using my Hunter Skills to scan for enemies." role played Jack.

After rolling a die held in his hand, Tom, the "Dungeon Master" explains:

"You find no trace of enemies. The woods seem thriving with life, however you sense no danger. "

" Tracy, It's your turn. "

Steve on more than one occasion was annoyed by Tracy's lack of attention. Most of the group appreciated her involvement, but as the newest member Steve often found her" Easily distracted nature" to be taxing.

"Oh, sorry guys. "" I move forward with the group. "

Tracy was a diminutive girl. She played the group's "rogue", upon Tom's suggestion. Whether it be because Jack genuinely thought she'd be a good addition to the group, or if he was simply trying to be friendly by asking her to join, no one was sure. Regardless, she had been a member for two previous adventures, both of which were "successful", at least according to Tom.

Steve's turn was next.

"Good move, Tracy. Helpful. " He said, sarcastically.

"Cool it, Steve." Jack said, half-heartedly.

"hold on guys, I think I dropped something back there. "

The group was now a few miles into the woods. It would be hard to find anything lost further on the trail, and the sun was going to set soon.

Tom momentarily regretted their choice of location for this adventure. He thought it would be a good idea to take a break from their usual routine of "Jack's backyard", so the group had joined him in his parent's old cabin, which was about twenty miles out of town. The Cabin was surrounded by woods, mostly deciduous trees. Tall oaks were the most notable.

Worried, "Do you want me to go with you?" said Jack.

"No, I'll be fine. " Tracy reassured.

The group, slightly flustered, decided to take a break at this point, per Tom's suggestion. Steve shrugs, and pulls out a granola bar from his pocket.

Tracy felt bad about lying to the group, but didn't want to explain the real reason she had felt the urge to seperate from the them.

Shortly before her turn, Tracy had seen something strange in the woods slightly off trail. It was a strange glow. No one else had seemed to notice it, so she pretended not to as well, for fear of seeming strange herself.

At first she ignored it, but before too long she had a feeling. It was if part of the woods was calling for her to investigate.

Before long she had come up with the excuse, and while she was still worried that it was not quite believable, she couldn't resist the feeling any longer.

So Tracy walked back to the spot where she had seen the strange glow, to where she was being called. The rest of the group did not question her, although Jack worried about her going off by herself, and Steve was annoyed by the delay.

It was only a few minutes before Tracy had returned to the spot. At first she saw nothing.

"Maybe I'm just going crazy." she thought to herself.

Then the feeling came back, stronger.

Tracy looked to where the glow was before, but saw nothing. She turned, scanning the woods.

There!

A soft glow on the opposite side of the trail as before.

From behind a large oak floated a single blue butterfly. It glowed, a radioactive blue that was distinct from the surroundings. From it originated the feeling of calling.

Tracy moved towards the butterfly, half in response to the feeling, and half out of curiosity.

The butterfly moved back, and Tracy began to walk off the trial. It moved seamlessly between the trees and around foliage, almost seeming to shimmer as it went. It was hard for Tracy to keep track of it.

Eventually it was gone.

Tracy looked around, now worried. She had followed this butterfly for what seemed like miles. Surely she was now lost.

She looked around. She had felt as if she was moving in a daze, and her surroundings were just now fading into her consciousness.

She was standing at the edge of a pond. Crystal blue water, that contrasted with what before had seemed like a pale green and brown woods. Now as she looked, the woods were thicker. More vibrant, more alive.

A sound came from behind Tracy, but it did not startle her. It was as if everything here was at utter peace.

A deer came from the bushes to her left. As it came it glanced at her, but moved forward as if she wasn't there. Mere feet away from her it took a sip from the pond.

More wildlife joined it. A rabbit, a fox, and even a small bear all one after the other came and joined her in this place.

Tracy felt nether fear nor confusion. She was more calm than she had ever been before.

Soon the butterfly was back, still glowing softly.

Tracy blinked.

Startled, she sat up. She was unsure if she had fallen asleep, but she was worried that the group had been waiting for her, or worse had left without her.

She looked around. She was on the trail, not far from where the group was waiting.

She ran back, and when she saw the group relief washed over her.

"That was fast. " Said Steve.

" Did you find what you were looking for? " asked Jack.

" Uh... How long was I gone? " asked Tracy?

To her, it felt as of she had been gone for hours, lost in the peaceful grove. At the very least she believed that it had been a dream, and that she must've been asleep for at least half an hour.

" Less than five minutes. " said Tom, looking at her quizzically.

" Uh.. Yeah I found it. Now where were we? "

The group continued with their Role playing, and Tracy did not think about the Grove again. As curious as the experience was, it had to have been a dream.

Meanwhile, a blue butterfly floated along in the woods.
